content.value_statement: Choosing a domain is slow when names are taken or hard to compare. This skill generates brandable options and guides availability checks across relevant TLDs.
actual_capabilities: Generates domain ideas from project descriptions and target audiences.
Compares options across .com, .io, .dev, .ai, .app, .co, and other TLDs.
Explains naming strengths such as length, memorability, audience fit, and brand fit.
Suggests variations when preferred names are taken or too expensive.
Provides workflows for startup launches, personal brands, and product naming.
Adds pricing context for standard domains, premium TLDs, and taken domains.
limitations: The skill files do not include a registrar API or automated WHOIS client.
Availability and prices can change, so users should verify before purchase.
Trademark and legal checks require separate professional review.
Social handle availability requires current research outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Name a Startup
use_cases.description: Generate short, brandable domain options for a new company and compare practical TLD choices.

use_cases.title: Launch a Product
use_cases.description: Find product domain names that match the audience, category, and launch positioning.

use_cases.title: Build a Personal Brand
use_cases.description: Create professional domain variations using a name, role, niche, or portfolio focus.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Domain Ideas
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a simple project description.
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest domain names for my project. It is a task manager for remote teams.

prompt_templates.title: Add TLD Preferences
prompt_templates.scenario: Focus the search on preferred extensions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Brainstorm short domain names for my AI writing assistant. Prefer .ai, .io, and .com options.

prompt_templates.title: Use Keywords and Positioning
prompt_templates.scenario: Include required words and brand direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest domain names for a design studio using pixel or studio. Keep the names modern and easy to spell.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Patterns and Alternatives
prompt_templates.scenario: Analyze a market category before generating names.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review naming patterns used by project management tools. Then suggest similar available-style domains with .com, .io, and .dev options.

output_examples.input: I am building a developer tool for sharing code snippets.
output: snippet.dev: Strong fit for developers, short, and easy to remember.
codeclip.io: Clear action-oriented name with a common startup TLD.
snippetbox.com: Descriptive .com option with a practical brand feel.

output_examples.input: I need a name for a sustainable fashion brand.
output: wearrenew.com: Simple, memorable, and aligned with sustainability.
threadwise.eco: Clear category signal with a values-focused TLD.
wovenagain.fashion: Descriptive option for a circular fashion audience.

best_practices: Verify availability with a registrar before choosing a final name.
Check trademarks and social handles before public launch.
Prioritize names that are short, pronounceable, and easy to spell.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on a domain suggestion without current availability checks.
Do not choose names that are hard to pronounce or explain.
Do not ignore trademark conflicts when a name feels available.

faq.question: Can this skill register domains?
faq.answer: No. It helps brainstorm and compare names, but registration happens through a domain registrar.

faq.question: Does it check live availability automatically?
faq.answer: The skill guides availability checks, but it does not include a built-in registrar or WHOIS integration.

faq.question: Which TLDs does it support?
faq.answer: It covers common options such as .com, .io, .dev, .ai, .app, .co, .xyz, .design, and .tech.

faq.question: Can it help with non-English names?
faq.answer: Yes. It can brainstorm multilingual options when the user provides target languages and audience context.

faq.question: Does it replace trademark research?
faq.answer: No. It can remind users to check trademarks, but legal review requires a qualified professional.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Founders, product teams, creators, agencies, and developers can use it before choosing a project or brand domain.
